question: Which legendary sprinter was named a Guinness World Records ICON in June 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Usain Bolt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Usain Bolt**, the **Jamaican** sprinting legend, was named a **Guinness World Records ICON** in **June 2025** (marking a milestone anniversary of his peak achievements) for his unprecedented dominance and lasting impact on **Track and Field**. *Hence, option B is correct.*
 
• He is the world record holder in the **100 metres**, **200 metres**, and the **4 × 100 metres relay**, making him the **fastest man in history**. His 100m record of **9.58 seconds** and 200m record of **19.19 seconds** were both set at the **2009 World Athletics Championships** in **Berlin**, **Germany**.
 
• **Usain Bolt** has secured a total of **8 Olympic gold medals** and is the only sprinter to win the **Olympic 100m and 200m titles** at three consecutive **Olympics** (**Beijing 2008**, **London 2012**, and **Rio 2016**).
 
• The title of **Guinness World Records ICON** is reserved for individuals whose achievements are so significant that they redefine their field; Bolt holds the record for the **most IAAF World Championship gold medals** won by a male athlete (**11 gold medals**).
 
• Other athletes mentioned like **Justin Gatlin**, **Carl Lewis**, and **Michael Johnson** are legends in their own right, but they do not hold the specific **ICON** status designated for this timeframe or the current world records in the primary sprint categories. *Hence, options A, C, and D are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Guinness World Records (GWR):** Originally known as the **Guinness Book of Records**, it was first published in **1955** by the **Guinness Brewery**. It serves as the primary international authority on **record-breaking achievements** across human and natural categories.
 
• **Justin Gatlin:** An **American** sprinter who was a major rival to Bolt. He won the **Olympic 100m gold** in **2004** and the **World Championship gold** in **2005** and **2017**. He is known for his longevity in the sport, competing well into his late **30s**.
 
• **Carl Lewis:** A former **American** track and field athlete who won **9 Olympic gold medals** and **8 World Championship gold medals**. He dominated the **100m**, **200m**, and **Long Jump** during the **1980s** and **1990s**.
 
• **Michael Johnson:** An **American** sprinter who specialized in the **200m** and **400m**. He held the 200m world record of **19.32 seconds** (set at the **1996 Atlanta Olympics**) for **12 years** until it was broken by **Usain Bolt** in **2008**.
 
• **Sprinting Physics:** During his 100m record run in **2009**, Bolt reached a **top speed** of **44.72 km/h** (**27.78 mph**), which remains the highest speed ever recorded for a human being on foot.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Berlin Breakthrough:** The **year 2009** remains the most significant in sprinting history, as the **100m** and **200m** world records were lowered by the largest margins since the introduction of **electronic timing**.
 
• **Retirement:** **Usain Bolt** officially retired from athletics after the **2017 World Championships** held in **London**. Following his track career, he briefly explored **professional football** in **Australia** and **Europe**.
 
• **Linguistic and Cultural Impact:** Bolt’s signature **"To Di World"** pose (often called the **lightning bolt**) became a global symbol of **victory** and **excellence**, contributing to his **ICON** status.
 
• **World Athletics:** Formerly known as the **IAAF** (International Association of Athletics Federations), it is the **international governing body** for the sport of **athletics**, which ratifies all sprint world records.
